chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: First teacher Manuel Roque; New Orleans bands at his father's shop
summary: Manuel Roque, a bricklayer from New Orleans, was his first clarinet teacher; visiting bands had their shoes fixed by his father, who knew Alphonse Picou.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Manuel Roque was my first clarinet teacher. Incidentally, he was from New Orleans, but he settled in Baton Rouge. Every time one of the bands from

New Orleans would come to play in Baton Rouge, which was very often, half of them would come to Papa's shop to have their shoes fixed. And half of them owed Papa money. Anybody that came to Papa's shoe shop and started talking about music, that was it. Papa loved music so much, especially a professional musician, he would do anything for them. So he'd fix their shoes, and that's how he happened to meet Alphonse Picou.
He didn't know him from anywhere else; just from coming to the store (or to your house).
Well, I think he had met people in New Orleans. But Papa used to go to New Orleans every week to buy leather supplies, and he knew a lot of those guys.
I was going to ask you, yeah, where he'd buy all the stuff for that. He went to New Orleans to buy that.
